items.name: Ghee Ven Pongal
steps: Rinse the rice and mung dal until the draining water is mostly clear; soak for 20 minutes and drain.
Warm the ghee in a heavy pot; bloom the cumin, ginger, and turmeric just until fragrant.
Add the drained grains and the prepared black pepper, coarsely crushed, cashews; turn them through the spiced fat for one minute.
Pour in the water, add the rock salt, and bring to a lively boil; lower the heat and cook covered for 30–35 minutes.
Stir and lightly press the grains to a cohesive, spoon-soft texture; rest covered for five minutes before serving warm.
items.guidance: Ghee Ven Pongal is a soft one-pot grain-and-pulse preparation suited to a freshly cooked meal. Vata: serve warm with a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor coriander or fennel and keep pungent seasoning mild. Kapha: use a lighter portion and sharpen gently with dry ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Vegetable Upma
steps: Prepare the semolina and cut the carrot, diced small and green peas and curry leaves evenly.
Warm the ghee and bloom the cumin and ginger until aromatic.
Add the main ingredient and vegetables, stir for one minute, then pour in the water.
Cook at a steady simmer until tender and cohesive; stir more often as the mixture thickens.
Season with rock salt, rest covered briefly, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Vegetable Upma is served freshly cooked and warm as a grain-based morning meal. Vata: make it softer and use a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor cooling aromatics and moderate sour garnish. Kapha: keep it light, dry, and modestly spiced.

items.name: Rava Idli
steps: Prepare the semolina as a thick, smooth batter with the water and yogurt.
Fold in the mustard seeds, curry leaves, sliced, fresh ginger, grated and rock salt; cover and rest for 45 minutes.
Grease the steaming molds lightly with ghee and fill each hollow no more than three-quarters full.
Steam over steady heat until the cakes are set through and spring back when touched.
Rest for two minutes, loosen the edges, and serve the steamed cakes warm.
items.guidance: Rava Idli is steamed rather than fried and is best eaten freshly made. Vata: serve warm with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: pair with a mild coconut or coriander chutney. Kapha: keep the cakes small and the accompaniment light.
items.reviewNote: Rava-idli leavening varies; this version relies on a well-rested yogurt batter and omits modern chemical raising agents that lack a verified ingredient link.

items.name: Pesarattu (Mung Dosa)
steps: Rinse the whole mung beans if whole, or sift it if flour; soak whole grains or pulses until pliable, then grind or whisk with the measured water to a smooth batter.
Stir in the cumin, ginger, rock salt, and green chili, finely chopped, fresh cilantro; rest the batter for 20 minutes after grinding.
Heat a heavy griddle and spread a thin film of ghee.
Pour and spread each pancake; cook until the surface sets, then turn and cook the second side.
Serve immediately while the center is tender and the edges are lightly crisp.
items.guidance: Pesarattu (Mung Dosa) is a griddle-cooked breakfast made from a rested grain or pulse batter. Vata: make smaller, softer pancakes and add ghee. Pitta: omit chilies and add coriander. Kapha: spread thinly and use minimal fat.

items.name: Adai (Mixed-Dal Dosa)
steps: Rinse the white rice if whole, or sift it if flour; soak whole grains or pulses until pliable, then grind or whisk with the measured water to a smooth batter.
Stir in the cumin, ginger, rock salt, and chana dal, toor dal, urad dal, curry leaves, sliced; rest the batter for 30 minutes after grinding.
Heat a heavy griddle and spread a thin film of ghee.
Pour and spread each pancake; cook until the surface sets, then turn and cook the second side.
Serve immediately while the center is tender and the edges are lightly crisp.
items.guidance: Adai (Mixed-Dal Dosa) is a griddle-cooked breakfast made from a rested grain or pulse batter. Vata: make smaller, softer pancakes and add ghee. Pitta: omit chilies and add coriander. Kapha: spread thinly and use minimal fat.

items.name: Besan Chilla
steps: Rinse the chickpea flour if whole, or sift it if flour; soak whole grains or pulses until pliable, then grind or whisk with the measured water to a smooth batter.
Stir in the cumin, ginger, rock salt, and fresh cilantro, chopped, ajwain seeds; rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy griddle and spread a thin film of ghee.
Pour and spread each pancake; cook until the surface sets, then turn and cook the second side.
Serve immediately while the center is tender and the edges are lightly crisp.
items.guidance: Besan Chilla is a griddle-cooked breakfast made from a rested grain or pulse batter. Vata: make smaller, softer pancakes and add ghee. Pitta: omit chilies and add coriander. Kapha: spread thinly and use minimal fat.

items.name: Moong Chilla
steps: Rinse the split mung dal if whole, or sift it if flour; soak whole grains or pulses until pliable, then grind or whisk with the measured water to a smooth batter.
Stir in the cumin, ginger, rock salt, and fresh cilantro; rest the batter for 20 minutes after grinding.
Heat a heavy griddle and spread a thin film of ghee.
Pour and spread each pancake; cook until the surface sets, then turn and cook the second side.
Serve immediately while the center is tender and the edges are lightly crisp.
items.guidance: Moong Chilla is a griddle-cooked breakfast made from a rested grain or pulse batter. Vata: make smaller, softer pancakes and add ghee. Pitta: omit chilies and add coriander. Kapha: spread thinly and use minimal fat.

items.name: Vermicelli Upma
steps: Prepare the semolina vermicelli and cut the carrot, diced small and green peas and curry leaves evenly.
Warm the ghee and bloom the cumin and ginger until aromatic.
Add the main ingredient and vegetables, stir for one minute, then pour in the water.
Cook at a steady simmer until tender and cohesive; stir more often as the mixture thickens.
Season with rock salt, rest covered briefly, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Vermicelli Upma is served freshly cooked and warm as a grain-based morning meal. Vata: make it softer and use a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor cooling aromatics and moderate sour garnish. Kapha: keep it light, dry, and modestly spiced.

items.name: Aloo Paratha
steps: Combine the whole-wheat flour, ajwain, rock salt, and cooked potato, mashed, fresh cilantro, chopped.
Add the water gradually and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into equal portions and roll each one evenly, dusting only as needed.
Cook on a hot griddle until both sides show brown speckles, brushing lightly with ghee as they finish.
Stack under a clean cloth and serve warm rather than holding them until dry.
items.guidance: Aloo Paratha is a freshly cooked griddle bread with restrained fat. Vata: serve soft with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: keep pungent fillings mild. Kapha: make it thin and use less finishing ghee.

items.name: Methi Paratha
steps: Combine the whole-wheat flour, ajwain, rock salt, and fresh fenugreek leaves, chopped.
Add the water gradually and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into equal portions and roll each one evenly, dusting only as needed.
Cook on a hot griddle until both sides show brown speckles, brushing lightly with ghee as they finish.
Stack under a clean cloth and serve warm rather than holding them until dry.
items.guidance: Methi Paratha is a freshly cooked griddle bread with restrained fat. Vata: serve soft with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: keep pungent fillings mild. Kapha: make it thin and use less finishing ghee.

items.name: Lauki Paratha
steps: Combine the whole-wheat flour, ajwain, rock salt, and bottle gourd, grated and squeezed, fresh cilantro.
Add the water gradually and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into equal portions and roll each one evenly, dusting only as needed.
Cook on a hot griddle until both sides show brown speckles, brushing lightly with ghee as they finish.
Stack under a clean cloth and serve warm rather than holding them until dry.
items.guidance: Lauki Paratha is a freshly cooked griddle bread with restrained fat. Vata: serve soft with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: keep pungent fillings mild. Kapha: make it thin and use less finishing ghee.

items.name: Lemon Poha
steps: Rinse the flattened rice briefly, drain, and rest it for five minutes so the flakes soften without becoming soggy.
Warm the ghee, pop the mustard seeds, and crisp the curry leaves.
Add the green peas, turmeric, and water; cover until the peas are tender.
Fold in the softened poha and rock salt and steam on low heat for four minutes.
Remove from the heat, add the lemon juice, and fluff gently before serving warm.
items.guidance: This poha is moistened gently and finished with lemon off the heat. Vata: use a little more ghee and keep the flakes soft. Pitta: halve the lemon and omit chilies. Kapha: retain the lemon and modest ghee.
items.reviewNote: Flattened rice is linked to its parent white-rice dravya because no standalone poha dravya or exact store item is available.

items.name: Ragi Porridge
steps: Whisk the finger millet flour with part of the water to make a lump-free slurry.
Bring the remaining water to a simmer and whisk in the slurry gradually.
Cook on low heat, stirring continuously, until the porridge loses its raw flour aroma and thickens.
Take the pot off the heat and let the porridge cool until lukewarm.
Whisk in the buttermilk, toasted cumin, and rock salt and serve immediately.
items.guidance: Cooked ragi is cooled to lukewarm before buttermilk is added for a savory summer porridge. Vata: serve slightly warmer and use less buttermilk. Pitta: retain the mild cumin and room-temperature serving. Kapha: dilute a little more and keep the portion moderate.

items.name: Spiced Oats Porridge
steps: Prepare the rolled oats and cut the cinnamon evenly.
Warm the ghee and bloom the cardamom until aromatic.
Add the main ingredient and vegetables, stir for one minute, then pour in the water.
Cook at a steady simmer until tender and cohesive; stir more often as the mixture thickens.
Season with rock sugar, rest covered briefly, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Spiced Oats Porridge is served freshly cooked and warm as a grain-based morning meal. Vata: make it softer and use a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor cooling aromatics and moderate sour garnish. Kapha: keep it light, dry, and modestly spiced.

items.name: Dalia (Broken Wheat) Porridge
steps: Rinse the broken wheat and drain well.
Warm the ghee in a heavy pot and toast the wheat until it smells nutty.
Add the water and simmer covered until the grains are nearly tender.
Pour in the milk and cook gently, stirring often, until the porridge is soft and creamy.
Stir in the rock sugar and cardamom, rest for three minutes, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Broken wheat is cooked first in water and then with milk for a soft breakfast porridge. Vata: retain the ghee and serve quite soft. Pitta: use less sugar and emphasize cardamom. Kapha: take a small portion and reduce ghee.

items.name: Thalipeeth (Multigrain)
steps: Combine the sorghum flour, ajwain, rock salt, and chickpea flour, whole-wheat flour, onion, finely chopped, fresh cilantro.
Add the water gradually and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into equal portions and roll each one evenly, dusting only as needed.
Cook on a hot griddle until both sides show brown speckles, brushing lightly with ghee as they finish.
Stack under a clean cloth and serve warm rather than holding them until dry.
items.guidance: Thalipeeth (Multigrain) is a freshly cooked griddle bread with restrained fat. Vata: serve soft with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: keep pungent fillings mild. Kapha: make it thin and use less finishing ghee.

items.name: Ragi Roti
steps: Combine the finger millet flour, ajwain, rock salt, and onion, finely chopped, curry leaves, finely sliced.
Add the water gradually and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into equal portions and roll each one evenly, dusting only as needed.
Cook on a hot griddle until both sides show brown speckles, brushing lightly with ghee as they finish.
Stack under a clean cloth and serve warm rather than holding them until dry.
items.guidance: Ragi Roti is a freshly cooked griddle bread with restrained fat. Vata: serve soft with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: keep pungent fillings mild. Kapha: make it thin and use less finishing ghee.

items.name: Bajra Roti with Gud-Ghee
steps: Combine the pearl millet flour and rock salt and add warm water gradually to form a soft dough.
Divide the dough and pat each portion between the palms or on a damp board into an even round.
Cook each roti on a hot griddle, turning carefully until both sides are cooked and lightly spotted.
Mix the jaggery with half the ghee to make a soft gud-ghee accompaniment.
Brush the rotis with the remaining ghee and serve warm with only a small dab of gud-ghee.
items.guidance: Warm bajra roti is paired with a deliberately small amount of gud-ghee in cold weather. Vata: retain the ghee and serve with a moist dal. Pitta: use less jaggery. Kapha: take one thin roti and omit extra gud-ghee.

items.name: Akki Roti
steps: Combine the white rice flour, ajwain, rock salt, and cucumber, grated and squeezed, fresh dill, chopped.
Add the water gradually and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into equal portions and roll each one evenly, dusting only as needed.
Cook on a hot griddle until both sides show brown speckles, brushing lightly with ghee as they finish.
Stack under a clean cloth and serve warm rather than holding them until dry.
items.guidance: Akki Roti is a freshly cooked griddle bread with restrained fat. Vata: serve soft with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: keep pungent fillings mild. Kapha: make it thin and use less finishing ghee.

items.name: Missi Roti
steps: Combine the chickpea flour, ajwain, rock salt, and whole-wheat flour, fresh cilantro.
Add the water gradually and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into equal portions and roll each one evenly, dusting only as needed.
Cook on a hot griddle until both sides show brown speckles, brushing lightly with ghee as they finish.
Stack under a clean cloth and serve warm rather than holding them until dry.
items.guidance: Missi Roti is a freshly cooked griddle bread with restrained fat. Vata: serve soft with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: keep pungent fillings mild. Kapha: make it thin and use less finishing ghee.

items.name: Kuttu Roti (Fasting)
steps: Combine the buckwheat flour, ajwain, rock salt, and cooked potato, mashed.
Add the water gradually and knead to a soft dough; cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into equal portions and roll each one evenly, dusting only as needed.
Cook on a hot griddle until both sides show brown speckles, brushing lightly with ghee as they finish.
Stack under a clean cloth and serve warm rather than holding them until dry.
items.guidance: Kuttu Roti (Fasting) is a freshly cooked griddle bread with restrained fat. Vata: serve soft with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: keep pungent fillings mild. Kapha: make it thin and use less finishing ghee.

items.name: Jeera Rice
steps: Rinse the white basmati rice until the water runs nearly clear; soak for 15 minutes and drain.
Warm the ghee; bloom the cumin and gently cook the indian bay leaf for one minute.
Add the drained grain, measured water, and rock salt; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Rest off the heat for eight minutes, then lift the grains gently with a fork before serving.
items.guidance: Jeera Rice is a lightly seasoned grain dish served freshly cooked. Vata: add ghee and pair with a moist dal. Pitta: keep sour and pungent garnish modest. Kapha: reduce ghee and favor a vegetable-rich portion.

items.name: Peas Pulao
steps: Rinse the white basmati rice until the water runs nearly clear; soak for 15 minutes and drain.
Warm the ghee; bloom the cumin and gently cook the green peas and indian bay leaf and green cardamom for one minute.
Add the drained grain, measured water, and rock salt; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Rest off the heat for eight minutes, then lift the grains gently with a fork before serving.
items.guidance: Peas Pulao is a lightly seasoned grain dish served freshly cooked. Vata: add ghee and pair with a moist dal. Pitta: keep sour and pungent garnish modest. Kapha: reduce ghee and favor a vegetable-rich portion.

items.name: Mint Rice
steps: Rinse the white basmati rice until the water runs nearly clear; soak for 15 minutes and drain.
Warm the Coconut oil; bloom the cumin and gently cook the fresh mint, chopped and fresh coconut, grated for one minute.
Add the drained grain, measured water, and rock salt; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Rest off the heat for eight minutes, then lift the grains gently with a fork before serving.
items.guidance: Mint Rice is a lightly seasoned grain dish served freshly cooked. Vata: add ghee and pair with a moist dal. Pitta: keep sour and pungent garnish modest. Kapha: reduce ghee and favor a vegetable-rich portion.

items.name: Raw Mango Rice
steps: Rinse the white rice until the water runs nearly clear; soak for 15 minutes and drain.
Warm the Sesame oil; bloom the cumin and gently cook the raw green mango, grated and mustard seeds and curry leaves for one minute.
Add the drained grain, measured water, and rock salt; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Rest off the heat for eight minutes, then lift the grains gently with a fork before serving.
items.guidance: Raw Mango Rice is a lightly seasoned grain dish served freshly cooked. Vata: add ghee and pair with a moist dal. Pitta: keep sour and pungent garnish modest. Kapha: reduce ghee and favor a vegetable-rich portion.

items.name: Sesame Rice

Warm the Sesame oil; bloom the cumin and gently cook the sesame seeds, toasted and curry leaves for one minute.
Add the drained grain, measured water, and rock salt; bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on low heat until the liquid is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Rest off the heat for eight minutes, then lift the grains gently with a fork before serving.

items.name: Millet-Curd Rice (Cooling)
steps: Rinse the millet and cook it with the water until soft; spread it in a wide bowl to cool until lukewarm.
Whisk the yogurt with the rock salt until smooth.
Fold the yogurt and cucumber through the lukewarm millet.
Warm the coconut oil, pop the mustard seeds, and crisp the curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the millet-curd mixture and serve at cool room temperature, never ice-cold.
items.guidance: Soft millet is cooled before yogurt and cucumber are folded in for this hot-season grain bowl. Vata: serve closer to warm and reduce cucumber. Pitta: retain the mild seasoning. Kapha: increase the millet-to-yogurt dilution and keep the portion small.
items.reviewNote: Regional millet-curd preparations use little, barnyard, or other small millets; proso millet is used because it has an exact dravya link.

items.name: Curd Oats Bowl
steps: Cook the oats with the water and rock salt until soft but not gluey.
Spread the oats in a bowl and let them cool until lukewarm.
Whisk the yogurt smooth and fold it through the oats.
Warm the ghee, pop the mustard seeds, and crisp the cumin and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the bowl and serve at room temperature.
items.guidance: Yogurt is folded into fully cooked, cooled oats for a savory breakfast bowl. Vata: serve less cool and add a little ghee. Pitta: keep spices mild. Kapha: use more water in the oats and a smaller yogurt portion.

items.name: Navratri Fasting Thali
steps: Mix the buckwheat flour with half the rock salt and enough water to make a soft dough; rest for ten minutes.
Shape small flatbreads and cook them on a griddle with half the ghee.
Warm the remaining ghee and cumin, add the potato and remaining salt, and cook covered with a splash of water until tender.
Whisk the yogurt and fold in the cucumber to make a plain raita.
Serve one warm buckwheat flatbread with the cumin potato and a small separate spoonful of raita.
items.guidance: This fasting plate combines buckwheat bread, cumin potato, and a simple cucumber raita in moderate portions. Vata: serve the bread soft with ghee and reduce raw cucumber. Pitta: keep cumin mild and favor the raita. Kapha: take more buckwheat and less potato and yogurt.

items.name: Ghee-Roasted Makhana
steps: Prepare the lotus seeds (makhana) in small, even pieces.
Warm the ghee with cumin until aromatic.
Add the prepared ingredients and rock salt; cook over medium-low heat, turning frequently.
Continue until heated through with a dry, lightly crisp exterior, taking care not to scorch the spices.
Serve warm in a modest portion.
items.guidance: Ghee-Roasted Makhana is a warm, simply seasoned snack rather than a cold or deeply fried preparation. Vata: choose a small soft portion and add ghee if dry. Pitta: keep pepper and sour garnish low. Kapha: use minimal ghee and emphasize the toasted finish.

items.name: Warm Sprout Salad
steps: Rinse the mung sprouts and spread them in a steamer basket.
Steam until warmed through and just tender, about five minutes.
Warm the ghee with toasted cumin and fold it through the sprouts with rock salt.
Remove from the heat and add the lemon juice and cilantro.
Serve immediately while warm, not as a raw chilled salad.
items.guidance: Brief steaming makes this sprout salad warmer and softer than a raw version. Vata: steam longer and add a little ghee. Pitta: use less lemon. Kapha: keep the light texture and full cilantro.

items.name: Warm Corn Chaat
steps: Steam the corn kernels with the water until tender and drain well.
Warm the ghee with the toasted cumin and add the corn.
Toss for two minutes until the kernels are evenly hot.
Take the pan off the heat and fold in the black salt, lemon juice, and cilantro.
Serve warm in small bowls.
items.guidance: This corn chaat is steamed and served warm, with sour seasoning added only after cooking. Vata: cook the corn very tender and add ghee. Pitta: halve the lemon and black salt. Kapha: retain the light ghee measure and warm serving.

items.name: Roasted Chana Snack
steps: Prepare the cooked chickpeas, well dried and black salt and amchur in small, even pieces.
Warm the ghee with cumin until aromatic.
Add the prepared ingredients and rock salt; cook over medium-low heat, turning frequently.
Continue until heated through with a dry, lightly crisp exterior, taking care not to scorch the spices.
Serve warm in a modest portion.
items.guidance: Roasted Chana Snack is a warm, simply seasoned snack rather than a cold or deeply fried preparation. Vata: choose a small soft portion and add ghee if dry. Pitta: keep pepper and sour garnish low. Kapha: use minimal ghee and emphasize the toasted finish.

items.name: Baked Vegetable Cutlet
steps: Combine the mashed potato, carrot, peas, ground rice flakes, cilantro, cumin, and rock salt.
Rest the mixture for ten minutes so the rice flakes absorb excess moisture.
Shape into small flat cutlets and brush both sides lightly with ghee.
Bake on a heated tray, turning once, until the surfaces are golden and the centers are hot.
Rest for three minutes and serve warm.
items.guidance: These vegetable cutlets are bound with ground rice flakes and baked rather than deep-fried. Vata: serve with a moist chutney and do not overbake. Pitta: pair with coriander chutney without chili. Kapha: keep the cutlets small and lightly brushed.
items.reviewNote: Flattened rice is linked to its parent white-rice dravya because no standalone poha binding is available.

Warm the ghee and bloom the cumin and ginger until aromatic.
Add the main ingredient and vegetables, stir for one minute, then pour in the water.
Cook at a steady simmer until tender and cohesive; stir more often as the mixture thickens.
Season with rock salt, rest covered briefly, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Plain Semolina Upma is served freshly cooked and warm as a grain-based morning meal. Vata: make it softer and use a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor cooling aromatics and moderate sour garnish. Kapha: keep it light, dry, and modestly spiced.

items.name: Carrot Upma

Add the main ingredient and vegetables, stir for one minute, then pour in the water.

Warm the ghee and bloom the cumin and ginger until aromatic.

items.guidance: Green Pea Upma is served freshly cooked and warm as a grain-based morning meal. Vata: make it softer and use a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor cooling aromatics and moderate sour garnish. Kapha: keep it light, dry, and modestly spiced.

steps: Prepare the proso millet and cut the carrot, diced small and green beans, finely cut and curry leaves evenly.
Warm the ghee and bloom the cumin and ginger until aromatic.
Add the main ingredient and vegetables, stir for one minute, then pour in the water.
Cook at a steady simmer until tender and cohesive; stir more often as the mixture thickens.
Season with rock salt, rest covered briefly, and serve warm.

items.name: Barley Vegetable Breakfast Bowl
steps: Prepare the pearled barley and cut the carrot, diced and green peas evenly.
Warm the ghee and bloom the cumin and ginger until aromatic.
Add the main ingredient and vegetables, stir for one minute, then pour in the water.
Cook at a steady simmer until tender and cohesive; stir more often as the mixture thickens.
Season with rock salt, rest covered briefly, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Barley Vegetable Breakfast Bowl is served freshly cooked and warm as a grain-based morning meal. Vata: make it softer and use a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor cooling aromatics and moderate sour garnish. Kapha: keep it light, dry, and modestly spiced.

items.name: Rice-Mung Steamed Idli
steps: Prepare the white rice, soaked as a thick, smooth batter with the water.
Fold in the split mung dal, soaked, cumin seeds and rock salt; cover and rest for 40 minutes after grinding.
Grease the steaming molds lightly with ghee and fill each hollow no more than three-quarters full.
Steam over steady heat until the cakes are set through and spring back when touched.
Rest for two minutes, loosen the edges, and serve the steamed cakes warm.
items.guidance: Rice-Mung Steamed Idli is steamed rather than fried and is best eaten freshly made. Vata: serve warm with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: pair with a mild coconut or coriander chutney. Kapha: keep the cakes small and the accompaniment light.

items.name: Carrot Rava Idli
steps: Prepare the semolina as a thick, smooth batter with the water and yogurt.
Fold in the carrot, finely grated, mustard seeds, curry leaves and rock salt; cover and rest for 45 minutes.
Grease the steaming molds lightly with ghee and fill each hollow no more than three-quarters full.
Steam over steady heat until the cakes are set through and spring back when touched.
Rest for two minutes, loosen the edges, and serve the steamed cakes warm.
items.guidance: Carrot Rava Idli is steamed rather than fried and is best eaten freshly made. Vata: serve warm with ghee and a moist accompaniment. Pitta: pair with a mild coconut or coriander chutney. Kapha: keep the cakes small and the accompaniment light.

Stir in the cumin, ginger, rock salt, and spinach, finely chopped, fresh cilantro; rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy griddle and spread a thin film of ghee.
Pour and spread each pancake; cook until the surface sets, then turn and cook the second side.
Serve immediately while the center is tender and the edges are lightly crisp.
items.guidance: Spinach Mung Chilla is a griddle-cooked breakfast made from a rested grain or pulse batter. Vata: make smaller, softer pancakes and add ghee. Pitta: omit chilies and add coriander. Kapha: spread thinly and use minimal fat.

items.name: Masoor Dal Chilla
steps: Rinse the red lentils if whole, or sift it if flour; soak whole grains or pulses until pliable, then grind or whisk with the measured water to a smooth batter.
Stir in the cumin, ginger, rock salt, and fresh cilantro, coriander seeds; rest the batter for 15 minutes.

Pour and spread each pancake; cook until the surface sets, then turn and cook the second side.

items.name: Barley Cinnamon Porridge
steps: Prepare the cracked barley and cut the cinnamon evenly.
Warm the ghee and bloom the cardamom until aromatic.
Add the main ingredient and vegetables, stir for one minute, then pour in the water.
Cook at a steady simmer until tender and cohesive; stir more often as the mixture thickens.
Season with rock sugar, rest covered briefly, and serve warm.
items.guidance: Barley Cinnamon Porridge is served freshly cooked and warm as a grain-based morning meal. Vata: make it softer and use a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor cooling aromatics and moderate sour garnish. Kapha: keep it light, dry, and modestly spiced.

items.name: Warm Puffed Rice Morning Chivda
steps: Warm the ghee in a wide pan and pop the mustard seeds.
Add the peanuts and curry leaves and cook until the peanuts smell toasted.
Stir in the turmeric and rock salt, then immediately add the puffed rice.
Turn continuously over low heat until every grain is warm and lightly crisp.
Serve at once before the chivda loses its fresh crunch.
